_comment: STARTER DATA — VERIFY BEFORE THE DEMO. South Florida native plants with a one-line wildlife payoff. Check every name and claim against UF/IFAS, the Atlas of Florida Plants (https://florida.plantatlas.usf.edu/) and the Florida Native Plant Society before relying on it. Note: the non-native Hamelia patens var. glabra ('African firebush') is also sold as firebush and would match the native entry here. Synonyms are older or alternate names a model may return.

species.why: Atala butterfly caterpillars eat only this plant. The butterfly was once thought extinct in Florida.
Tubular red flowers feed hummingbirds and zebra longwing butterflies, and its berries feed songbirds.
Drought-tolerant native grass that shelters ground-feeding birds and holds soil without fertilizer or irrigation.
Native milkweed that monarch and queen butterfly caterpillars need to survive.
Wet-soil native milkweed that hosts monarch and queen butterfly caterpillars.
Flowers feed hundreds of pollinator species, and its berries feed bears, deer and birds.
Florida's state tree: it rides out hurricanes and its fruit feeds birds, raccoons and bats.
One of the most important plants for wildlife here. Its leaves feed hundreds of kinds of caterpillars, which birds feed their chicks.
Holds dunes together against storm erosion, and its fruit feeds birds and other wildlife.
Salt-tolerant coastal tree that buffers storm surge and shelters wading birds.
Its roots break storm surge and shelter the juvenile fish that support Florida's fisheries.
Shade-tolerant shrub whose flowers feed pollinators and whose red berries feed birds.
Salt-tolerant hedge whose fruit feeds birds and small mammals.
Purple berries feed mockingbirds and other songbirds through fall and winter.
One of the most hurricane-tolerant native trees, and its fruit fuels migrating birds.
Caterpillars of the zebra longwing (Florida's state butterfly) and the gulf fritillary eat its leaves.
A Florida state wildflower (Coreopsis) that feeds native bees and butterflies.
Clumping grass that filters runoff and holds pond and ditch banks in place.
Caterpillars of skipper butterflies eat its leaves, and its thick clumps hold soil on slopes.
Tough, salt-tolerant shrub whose winter berries feed birds when other food is scarce.
Fragrant flowers feed pollinators and its orange berries feed birds; a hurricane-tolerant hedge.
